questions.question: How do you read a Ruby stack trace?
questions.title: Reading a Ruby Stack Trace
questions.direct_answer: A stack trace shows the chain of calls that led to an error, most-recent-call-last (bottom = where it failed; top = entry). Read it bottom-up: the last line is the error type + message (NoMethodError: undefined method `empty?' for nil) — start there. The frames above it are the call chain, each with a file:line in method (posts_controller.rb:7 in show). The bottom-most frame is where the error raised; frames above show who called it. In Rails with many gems, skim past gem frames to find YOUR code (app/...). The line numbers are real — open the file:line. The message names the method and receiver (undefined method X for Y) — Y is what you called X on (often nil). Trace: read the message, find your file:line, see what was nil/wrong, and fix upstream.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know to read bottom-up (message last; bottom frame = where it raised; find your app/ file:line).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Reading top-down (entry first) and getting lost, or skipping the message (it names the method and receiver).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Read a trace bottom-up: the last line is the error message; the bottom frame is where it raised. Find your app/ file:line. The message names method + receiver (often nil).

sections.title: Reading a Trace
sections.content:
bottom-up: message last; bottom frame = where it raised; find your app/ file:line.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  E[error msg: NoMethodError ... for nil] --> F1[frame: posts_controller.rb:7 in show]
  F1 --> F2[higher frames: who called it]
  F2 --> G[skim gem frames; find app/]
```

sections.title: Reading a stack trace
sections.content:
```ruby
# A Ruby stack trace (most-recent-call-LAST):
#
#   app/models/post.rb:15:in `excerpt'        <- higher frame (caller)
#   app/controllers/posts_controller.rb:7:in `show'
#   ... (gem frames you can skim)
#   config.ru:5:in `block in <main>'          <- entry (top)
#
#   NoMethodError: undefined method `empty?' for nil   <- MESSAGE (start here; LAST line)

# READ BOTTOM-UP:
#   1. Last line  -> the message: undefined method `empty?' for nil
#      -> you called .empty? on nil. (receiver is nil)
#   2. Bottom-most frame -> where it raised: posts_controller.rb:7 in `show'
#      -> open app/controllers/posts_controller.rb line 7.
#   3. Frames above -> who called it (the call chain).
#
# In Rails, skim past gem frames (gems/...) to find YOUR code (app/...).
# Line numbers are real: open the file:line.
# The message names method + receiver: undefined method X for Y (Y is often nil).
# Fix upstream: why did @post return nil? (find, guard with &., or a default.)
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Reading top-down (entry first) and getting lost in gem frames.
Skipping the message — it names the method and receiver (the key clue).
Not opening the file:line (the line numbers are real).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A stack trace is most-recent-call-last: bottom = where it failed; top = entry.
Read bottom-up: the last line is the error type + message (start there).
The bottom-most frame is where the error raised (file:line in method).
In Rails, skim past gem frames to find YOUR code (app/...); line numbers are real.
The message names method + receiver (undefined method X for Y) — Y is often nil.
